title: Lower an infant car seat's carry handle: both hub buttons held in while it swings back
instruction: Lower the infant car seat's carry handle from its upright carry position back to its rear position over the head end, and leave it locked there. Do not move the seat. Then move both grippers clear.
context: Almost every newborn in the US rides home in a rear-facing infant seat, and the carrier with a swing handle is the usual first seat. There were 3,628,934 US births in 2024 (CDC NCHS FastStats, Births: Final Data for 2024, https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/fastats/births.htm, opened 2026-11-19). Parents move this handle several times a day, between carrying, the car and feeding. The handle turns only while both buttons, about 44 cm apart, stay pressed; let one go too early and it locks partway. Unlike the board's tasks of seating a carrier on its base until both latches engage, this task never touches the base: it is the carry handle and its two release buttons.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers at the near edge of the table (bases 61 cm apart), a fixed camera above. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top. One empty infant car seat (carrier) sized on the Graco SnugRide 35 Lite LX, foot end toward the robot, on the table with no base. Shell: rigid dark grey polypropylene tub, 4.3 kg, 70 cm long (x -1 to 69), 37 cm wide at the side walls, walls 25 cm tall, on two flat 70 x 5 x 3 cm runners; reclined seat back and seat cushion inside (no fabric pad, harness or canopy). Hub axis across the seat at x 29, 28 cm high. Each side: a hub boss (10 cm across) on the shell wall and, outboard of the handle arm, a fixed grey hub cap (2 x 5.1 cm radius, 4 mm thick) with a ring of holes 7 mm wide at 4.5 cm from the axis, at 0 (carry), 35, 65 and 85 degrees (rear) back from upright. Carry handle: rigid U-bar, 0.45 kg, dark grey plastic, arms 3.5 x 1.6 cm in section, arm centres 42.2 cm apart, top bar 3.2 cm thick 30 cm from the axis with a 16 cm black rubber grip; it turns back toward the head end from upright (0) to a stop at 86 degrees; at the start it is upright, locked in the carry holes. Release buttons (orange plastic, one per arm): a 1.5 x 2.5 cm cap 6 mm proud of the arm's outer face, its centre 10 cm up the arm from the axis, joined by a stem to a 5 x 5 mm lock pin at 4.5 cm from the axis. A spring (1.5 N at rest, 10.5 N pressed) holds the pin 4 mm deep in a hub cap hole; pressed 6 mm, the pin is clear and the handle turns. Released between holes, the pin rides on the cap and drops into the next hole it reaches. Start (seeded): the seat is moved up to 4 cm along x and 0.6 cm along y and turned up to 6 degrees about the vertical, redrawn until one handle arm's grip point is at least 2.5 cm off its place in the screenshot along x. The screenshot shows seed 0.
scoring: Scored at the end. Tools: protractor sticker on the hub, ruler, tape outline of the seat, 30 fps video. Angle: 0.5 x (handle angle back from upright - 5) / 80 degrees, from 0 at 5 degrees; the full 0.5 within 3 degrees of the rear position (85). Locked: +0.3 if at the rear position both buttons are fully out (pressed in less than 1 mm of 6, so both pins sit in their rear holes). Seat still: +0.2 if also locked and the seat moved under 30 mm, turned under 5 degrees and tilts under 5 degrees from its start outline. Examples: rear and locked, seat still 1.0; rear and locked, seat dragged 0.8; stopped locked at the 65 degree hole 0.38, at 35 degrees 0.19; never turned 0. Score 0 if at any time the handle was more than 2.5 degrees off a lock position while a button was pressed in less than 2 mm (its pin at least 2 mm deep: the lock was forced), or if a gripper ends less than 10 mm from the handle or a button (it must have let go).
reset_notes: Press both buttons, turn the handle back to upright until both pins click into the carry holes, and set the seat back on its taped outline. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Official yam_arena simulator (PhysX), 20 Hz. Rigid shell and handle at real size and mass. Buttons are sprung slide joints; the lock is plain contact of each pin in the hub cap holes, no rule. Simplified: viscous hinge damping for dry friction; a joint stop for the handle's rest on the head end; no fabric; button 40 g. Not maker data: the buttons' place (10 cm up each arm, where a gripper can squeeze them against the arm), pin and hole sizes, the 35 and 65 degree holes.
scores: Dream-1 run, seed 0: 0.0 (1,200 steps). Scripted demo, reads object poses from the simulator: 1.0 on seeds 0, 1 and 2 (342 steps each). Wrong outcomes on seed 0: fixed plan 0.0; a button let go early 0.38; no button pressed 0.0; hands left on the handle 0.0.
